correctness.rationale: For even \(m\), induction gives \(F(m)\le2\phi(m)-1\). For a hypothetical perfect totient \(3^k p\), the exact identity \(F(2\cdot3^{k-1}(p-1))=3^{k-1}(p+2)\) and the factorization \(p-1=2^a3^b u\) give \(\phi(m)=2\cdot3^{k-2}(p-1)\phi(u)/u\). Substitution and cancellation yield the strict claimed bound. Multiplicativity then turns it into the prime-support product condition. The three congruence exclusions use exact products \(24/35\), \(8/11\), and \(48/65\), each below \(3/4\). The bundled finite checker directly replays definitions on a bounded domain and is explicitly not used as the infinite proof.

residual_risks: The 1939 Pérez-Cacho article and the 1982 Mohan–Suryanarayana article were not directly available for full-text inspection in this run. value.rationale: The literature explicitly leaves the existence of perfect totients \(3^k p\) for \(k\ge4\) open. The claim converts that motivated open family into a uniform, exponent-independent support barrier on \(p-1\), excluding whole infinite congruence classes such as \(p\equiv1\pmod{35}\), \(p\equiv1\pmod{55}\), and \(p\equiv1\pmod{65}\). This is a structural sieve useful for both theoretical case reduction and searches, rather than an arbitrary finite computation or a renamed textbook identity.
